$comment: The accessibility contract as data. The four load-bearing fields of a row — `fg`, `bg`, `label`, `min` — are the same four values samourai-visio/scripts/check-contrast.py carries in the `PAIRINGS` tuples it hardcodes; that script reads no JSON and this file is not an input to it. The shape is deliberate all the same, so a pairing can move from there to here without being reinterpreted. `fg` and `bg` are token paths from tokens.json, or a literal #hex. `min` is 4.5 for text (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3) or 3.0 for a non-text boundary, control edge or focus indicator (SC 1.4.11); the large-text 3:1 exemption is not used anywhere in this system. `fgAlpha` composites the foreground over the background before measuring — a translucent colour measured as if it were opaque reports a ratio no user ever sees. `exempt` records a row that is measured and reported but not gated. `expect: "fail"` inverts the row: it is a pair the design system forbids, and the gate fails if it ever starts passing, because that means the palette moved under the rule.

slate-500 as running text — forbidden by DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §2; slate.500 is the placeholder and picto step, and the two text.placeholder rows are exempt only because a placeholder is never real text. This row fails the gate if it ever starts passing

a -500 status colour as text on white — forbidden by DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §2; the -500 step is for dots and fills, the -600 step is the text. green.500 at 4.25:1 is the step closest to the line, so it crosses first. This row fails the gate if it ever starts passing

the same §2 rule on the second of the three status colours: amber.500 as text on white, 3.64:1 today. red.500 is the third and is the one no contrast row can carry — it already clears 4.5:1 at 5.42:1, so an expect-fail row for it would fail on the day it was added. For red, "the -500 step is not text" is a semantic rule and needs a lint over product code
